summary: REQ-10 is largely implemented end-to-end (II-gated UI per file summaries, user discovery excluding self, client-side encrypt-before-send and decrypt-after-fetch, polling refresh, and privacy UI for deleting messages/conversations and clearing local keys). However, backend deletion semantics for both deleteMessage and deleteConversation appear incomplete/incorrect relative to the acceptance criteria (conversation deletion does not remove all messages with the contact; message deletion is not clearly restricted to the sender and may not match messages where the caller was the sender vs recipient). The diff also introduces an unrequested admin-token/access-control initialization path.

missing_requirements.requirement: The sender can delete a message and it is removed from future fetches.
missing_requirements.reason: Backend deleteMessage only filters out messages where msg.recipient == recipient and msg.timestamp == timestamp, and does not check msg.sender == caller. This may fail to delete messages sent by the caller depending on how recipient is passed, and does not enforce 'sender-only' deletion as specified.

missing_requirements.requirement: The user can delete a conversation using the existing privacy menu without breaking the app.
missing_requirements.reason: Backend deleteConversation filters only messages where msg.sender == caller and msg.recipient == recipient, leaving messages sent by the other participant intact; this does not appear to delete the full 1:1 conversation from future fetches for the caller.

hallucinated_features.description: Admin secret token extraction from URL/session and initialization of backend access control using a `caffeineAdminToken` parameter.
hallucinated_features.reason: REQ-10 does not mention admin tokens or access-control bootstrapping via URL parameters; this adds unrelated auth/config behavior.
Not requested by REQ-10 and introduces additional authorization framework beyond Internet Identity gating described in the requirement.
